### ① Derived judgments

**Triage note 1 — the node respelled, the rest of the example in line with the declared element.** Met. The README's "Schema-Driven Usage" block now reads `type: 'timeline'`; that line is the whole diff on the page. The rest of the block was checked key by key against the head's `TimelineSchema` (`packages/types/src/data-display.ts`, interface `TimelineSchema`) and its zod twin (`packages/types/src/zod/data-display.zod.ts`, `TimelineSchema` and `TimelineFeedItemSchema`): `variant: 'vertical'` is in the `variant` enum and selects the feed arm in `timelineItemsFitVariant`; the one item carries `time`, `title`, `description` and `variant: 'success'`, all four declared on `TimelineFeedItem`, `title` being the arm's required key, and `success` a member of `TimelineItemVariant`. No item carries `date`, `label` or a nested `items`, so the arm refinement is satisfied. `dateFormat` and `scale` are not written and default. The retired `events`, `orientation` and `position` appear nowhere in the README (the whole file was read, not only the block). The other sentences on the page were read against the head too: the opening sentence's "vertical, horizontal, and Gantt-style" matches the `variant` enum; "automatically registers with ObjectUI's component registry when imported" matches the two `ComponentRegistry.register('timeline', …)` calls in `packages/plugin-timeline/src`; the two `tsx` usage blocks import names the `README Export Check` gate verified as real exports; `TimelineMarker variant="success"` is a member of `timelineMarkerVariants`. No other false sentence found. The docs-site page `content/docs/plugins/plugin-timeline.mdx` already spells its example `type: 'timeline'`, so no sibling site needed the same edit.

**Accepted by `safeValidateSchema` and the strict face.** Yes, by reading: `AnyComponentSchema` is `z.discriminatedUnion('type', …)`, so the old block (no `type` key at all) fails at the discriminator with `invalid_union` at `type`, and the respelled block matches the `timeline` arm on every key it writes. `safeValidateSchema` is the call `packages/cli/src/commands/validate.ts` makes, so the card's "what `objectui validate` runs" premise holds. The strict authoring face closes every object to its declared keys (objectui#8345); the block writes only declared keys.

**Renders as documented through the real `SchemaRenderer`.** Judged by reading; the dev's runtime probe is consistent with what the tree says. The bare `timeline` key is claimed by `view:timeline` (`ObjectTimelineRenderer` in `packages/plugin-timeline/src/index.tsx`) because the presentational registration in `renderer.tsx` passes `skipFallback: true`. `ElementDataSourceGate` hands an unbound node straight to its child (no `requiresDataSource`, no `dataSource` key, so neither the missing nor the loading panel). `ObjectTimeline` treats authored `items` as a pass-through (`if (schema.items) return schema.items;`), `hasAuthoredItems` skips the date-axis refusal, and `effectiveSchema` spreads the node (so `variant` and the default `dateFormat`) into `TimelineRenderer`. The rendered text the dev quotes, `1/15/2024Project StartedKickoff meeting`, is the `short` date default over `2024-01-15` followed by the title and description, which is what that path draws. The old spelling has no `type`, so the registry lookup misses and `SchemaRenderer` paints the `Unknown component type:` panel, as the changeset says.

**The pin `packages/types/src/__tests__/timeline-readme-schema-example-10824.test.ts`.**
- It extracts on every run: `readFileSync` of `packages/plugin-timeline/README.md` resolved from the repo root, the section bounded by the exact heading line `## Schema-Driven Usage` and the next `#`/`##` heading, fence pairing through `openFence` / `closesFence` imported from `scripts/markdown-fence-scan.mjs` (the import carries the same `@ts-expect-error` line the sibling `packages/types` tests use for `js-comment-mask.mjs`), the `import` line dropped, and the literal evaluated with `new Function` and returned as `schema`. Nothing is mirrored in the test. A missing heading, a duplicated heading or an unclosed fence throws rather than skips, and the first `it` requires exactly one `const schema` block, so an empty extraction cannot pass.
- On the old spelling: both the tolerant and the strict leg fail with `invalid_union` at `type` (the discriminator is absent); the extraction leg stays green, so the red is the validator's, not the extractor's. On a stray unknown key at the root or inside an item: the tolerant face is `.passthrough()` and accepts it, the strict leg refuses it with `unrecognized_keys`, so that leg is live on its own. That matches the dev's ablation table; it was not re-executed here.
- Placement is sound. Two tests in `packages/types` already read a sibling plugin's README off disk in the same way: `calendar-flat-color-allday-8466.test.ts` (`readRepo(CALENDAR_README)` over `packages/plugin-calendar/README.md`) and `object-view-unmirrored-keys-7779.test.ts` (`packages/plugin-view/README.md`), and `plugin-timeline`'s own `metaFields` source pin sits in `plugin-list` for the stated reason. The premise holds against a census at the head: every `packages/plugin-*` test that imports `node:fs` lives in a package whose `tsconfig.test.json` names `node` in `types`, and `packages/plugin-timeline/tsconfig.test.json` names no `types` at all. `packages/types` also owns both faces the document is judged against. Not a boundary violation.
- The ledger row in `scripts/markdown-test-inputs.mjs` is correct and required: `deriveCandidates()` lifts the literal `packages/plugin-timeline/README.md` out of the test and would report an `unadjudicated-test` finding without a row; with the row, `--audit` at the head prints `103 candidate test files, all adjudicated; 76 declared entries, all present`, and `--changed packages/plugin-timeline/README.md` prints that path, so a README-only pull request reaches the shard.

The program that compiles this file is `packages/types/tsconfig.test.json`, whose `lib` is `ES2022`, so that clause is untrue where it sits (it was carried over from the dashboard README test, whose own test config is ES2022 as well). The choice it justifies, no try/catch so the evaluator's error names the unreadable token, stands on its first reason alone. Fix: delete the parenthetical, or say that this package's test program is ES2022 and the wrapper is omitted for loudness only.
